compiler_and_flags: GCC 11.5.0 (Xeon, Graviton 4), clang-20 (EPYC 7R13); CMake Release with add_compile_options(-Wall -Wextra -O3) plus per-ISA -m flags in CMakeLists.txt; compiler for the Apple M4 Max rows is not stated in BENCHMARKS.md
hardware: Apple M4 Max; Intel Xeon 6975P-C (AWS c8i, 2 vCPU); AWS Graviton 4 (c8g.large, pinned with taskset); AMD EPYC 7R13 (c6a, 2 vCPU)
name: PIVCO-Huffman
baseline: huf0 (zstd's Huffman decoder, from Cyan4973/FiniteStateEntropy, X1 and X2 variants) and Oodle newlz_arrays_huff
workload: Decode of a 4M-symbol Huffman-coded sequence repeated 100 times per run (median of 3 best of 5 runs), across 30 synthetic and real-world distributions, on Apple M4 Max NEON, Xeon 6975P-C AVX-512, Graviton 4 NEON and EPYC 7R13 AVX2/SSE.
claimed_speedup: README: proba80 15.3 GB/s, 5.9x huf0_x2; proba50/proba14 9.2/5.2 GB/s, 3.6x/2.1x; flat_M* 20-24 GB/s, 4.1-4.8x; real text 4.3-4.8 GB/s, 2.0-2.5x huf0_x2. docs/BENCHMARKS.md M4 Max table: english 6142 vs huf0 X2 2414 (units as in table), vs-best 2.55x. Cross-ISA peak ratios 1.43-13.8x (Xeon AVX-512), 0.94-22.5x (Zen 3, three real-text rows lose by about 6%).
tradeoffs: Own block-based wire format (4096-8192 symbol blocks, not drop-in compatible with Huffman streams); encoded size within 1-4% of ordinary Huffman; PHA variant trades decode bandwidth for ratio (8.45x vs 6.40x on proba80). Needs NEON, AVX2 or AVX-512; builds FSE as a submodule for PHA.
caveats: README itself marks the project WIP and not production-ready; BENCHMARKS.md says 'Last content review: NEVER'. Some table cells show 0 for huf0 (cannot encode those distributions). Author's own benchmark (A rests on public code plus stated compilers/CPUs, not independent). Oodle baseline needs a licensed SDK symlinked into ext/oodle so those rows may not be reproducible by others. 'vs best' ratios for Zen 3 include losses. Paper at marcinzukowski.github.io not opened (github.io blocked).

name: FiniteStateEntropy (FSE and Huff0)
baseline: zlibh (the Huffman encoder inside zlib, extracted by Frederic Kayser)
workload: Entropy compress and decompress synthetic files Proba80, Proba14, Proba02 generated by probagen, split into 32 KB blocks.
claimed_speedup: Proba80 decompression: Huff0 1350 MB/s, FSE 440 MB/s, zlibh 300 MB/s (Huff0 about 4.5x, derived from page data); compression Huff0 600, FSE 325, zlibh 265 MB/s. Proba14 decompression Huff0 860, FSE 460, zlibh 250 MB/s. Proba02 decompression Huff0 555, FSE 445, zlibh 210 MB/s. FSE ratio 8.84 versus 6.38 for Huffman on Proba80.
stars_or_usage: 1.5k stars; FSE and Huff0 are the entropy stage of zstd
tradeoffs: FSE (tANS) reaches arithmetic-coding-level ratio but is slower than Huff0; on flat distributions FSE gives little gain over Huffman. Huff0 limited by Huffman 1-bit-per-symbol floor.
caveats: Benchmark is old (GCC 4.8.4, 2015-era laptop CPU), flags unstated, synthetic test files. The code is also vendored into zstd (already catalogued as facebook/zstd), so this entry is the standalone entropy library. Recent commits are CI-only. Reported because the repo is the canonical Huff0/FSE source and the only named baseline is zlib's Huffman.
